title: CORNER Spec Amendments: C3/C4/C5 Gaps
summary: Gaps and amendments identified in C3, C4, and C5 specs after writing C6 and C7. Backward-looking review. Things the later specs revealed that the earlier specs missed or underspecified.
content:
CORNER Spec Amendments: C3/C4/C5

Author: Steve (AI Advisory Lead) Date: 2026-03-16 Purpose: Writing C6 and C7 revealed gaps in the earlier specs. This document captures amendments that should be applied to C3, C4, and C5 before Bobby builds them. These aren't rewrites. They're patches.

C3 Amendments

Amendment 3.1: WebSocket Protocol Needs Versioning

The gap: C3's WebSocket protocol defines event types and JSON schemas but has no version field. When C4 adds new event types (connection_info, sync_state) and C6 adds SDK access, the protocol needs backward compatibility. If we don't version from C3, every protocol change breaks every connected client until they refresh.

Amendment: Add "protocol_version": "1" to the initial WebSocket handshake response. Client includes the version it supports in the connection request. Server responds with the highest mutually supported version. This is a 2-line addition in C3 but saves weeks of migration pain in C4-C6.

// Client handshake request
{ "type": "auth", "jwt": "...", "protocol_version": "1" }

// Server handshake response
{ "type": "connection_accepted", "protocol_version": "1", "supported_versions": ["1"] }

Bobby should implement this in C3 Step 1. Negligible effort now. Enormous value later.

Amendment 3.2: Task Data Model Needs assigned_to Field

The gap: C3's Checklist mode has a task model with automation_id (agent), position, status, text. It assumes one human user per office. C7 introduces multi-user and assigns tasks to team members, not just agents. If the schema doesn't include assigned_to from day one, adding it later requires a migration on every client's database.

Amendment: Add to the Supabase tasks table schema in C3 Step 4:

  • assigned_to (uuid, nullable, FK to auth.users). Null = assigned to agent only (current behavior). Populated = assigned to a human user.
  • created_by (uuid, nullable, FK to auth.users). Tracks who created the task.

These columns are nullable and ignored until C7. Zero impact on C3-C6 behavior. But the schema is ready for multi-user when the time comes.

Amendment 3.3: XP Data Model Needs source Field

The gap: C3's XP data model logs events with event_type (task_complete, commit, handoff_complete) but no source field. C7's Academy gives XP for completing courses. C7's multi-user needs XP tracked per user, not just per agent. The data model as written can't distinguish "agent completed task" from "user completed course" from "user completed task manually."

Amendment: Add to xp_events table:

  • source (text): "agent", "user", "academy", "milestone". Identifies what generated the XP.
  • user_id (uuid, nullable, FK to auth.users): which human user earned the XP (null for agent-only XP in C3-C6).

Amendment 3.4: Keyboard Shortcuts Need a Registry Pattern

The gap: C3 hardcodes keyboard shortcuts (1, 2, 3, Esc, /, T, ?, Cmd+K). C5 adds room editor shortcuts. C6 adds voice toggle. C7 adds Academy navigation. If shortcuts are hardcoded throughout components, conflicts become unmanageable.

Amendment: Bobby should implement a central keyboard shortcut registry in C3 Step 7 instead of scattering event listeners. A single useKeyboardShortcuts hook that:

  • Registers all shortcuts in one config object
  • Handles priority (modal shortcuts override global shortcuts)
  • Prevents conflicts (same key can't be registered twice)
  • Powers the ? overlay (reads from the registry, always up to date)
  • Extensible: future features register new shortcuts without touching existing code

This is a code architecture choice, not a feature addition. Bobby decides implementation. The spec just needs to call it out.

Amendment 3.5: Mini-Map Should Show Multi-User Presence (Future-Ready)

The gap: C3's mini-map shows agent status dots. C7 adds human user presence (avatars in the office). If the mini-map only renders agents, adding user dots later requires refactoring the rendering logic.

Amendment: Mini-map should render generic "entity" dots from a list, not hardcoded agent dots. The list includes agents now. In C7, it includes users too. Implementation is the same; just pass a different data source.

Amendment 3.6: Mobile Responsive Needs to Account for Chat Bar Height on Keyboard Open

The gap: C3's mobile spec mentions "keyboard avoidance on mobile chat input" as a single checkbox item. This is actually the #1 mobile UX killer in chat-based apps. When the virtual keyboard opens on iOS, the entire viewport shifts unless handled correctly. The chat bar needs to remain visible and the message input needs to stay above the keyboard.

Amendment: Add explicit spec for Bobby:

  • Use visualViewport API to detect actual viewport height (not window.innerHeight which includes keyboard area on iOS Safari)
  • Chat bar anchored to bottom of visual viewport, not bottom of document
  • When keyboard opens: game view shrinks, chat bar stays at keyboard top, message history scrolls to show latest message
  • Test on iPhone SE (smallest screen, worst case) and iPhone Pro Max (largest)
  • This must pass Elmo QA on both devices before shipping

C4 Amendments

Amendment 4.1: Container Health Check Needs CC Session Verification

The gap: C4's health check endpoint verifies the container is running (HTTP 200 on port 3002). It doesn't verify that the Claude Code session inside the container is functional. A container can be "healthy" (Node.js WS bridge running) while CC is crashed, hung, or rate-limited.

Amendment: Health check should have two levels:

  • Level 1 (infrastructure): WS bridge server is running, port 3001 accepting connections. This is what the current spec describes.
  • Level 2 (functional): CC session responds to a test prompt within 30 seconds. Run a lightweight "ping" skill that returns a known response. If CC doesn't respond, health status = "degraded" (not "down", because the WS bridge is still serving cached data).

Health check endpoint response:

{
  "status": "healthy",       // "healthy" | "degraded" | "down"
  "ws_bridge": "running",
  "cc_session": "responsive", // "responsive" | "unresponsive" | "rate_limited"
  "last_cc_response": "2026-03-16T14:30:00Z",
  "uptime_seconds": 3600
}

Admin panel shows degraded containers with yellow status. Auto-restart CC session if unresponsive for 5 minutes.

Amendment 4.2: Provisioning Needs Rollback on Partial Failure

The gap: C4's provisioning flow is a linear pipeline (create Supabase records > write files > start container > register endpoint). If step 5 fails (container won't start), steps 1-4 have already committed. There's orphaned data in Supabase and a workspace volume with no container.

Amendment: Provisioning should be transactional with rollback:

  • Each step records what it created
  • If any step fails, previous steps are reversed
  • Supabase records deleted, workspace volume removed, DNS entry purged
  • Client sees: "Setup encountered an issue. Retrying..." (automatic retry once)
  • If retry fails: "We're setting up your office manually. You'll receive an email within 1 hour." (AOM admin alert triggers)

This is standard infrastructure hygiene but the spec doesn't call it out.

Amendment 4.3: WebSocket Bridge Needs Message Ordering Guarantees

The gap: C4's WebSocket bridge sends events as they occur. Over the internet, events can arrive out of order (especially during reconnection when queued events are replayed). A task_complete event arriving before its task_created event makes the UI show a completed task that was never created.

Amendment: Add sequence numbers to all WebSocket events:

{
  "type": "task_complete",
  "seq": 1847,
  "agent": "bobby",
  ...
}

Client tracks the last received sequence number. On reconnect, requests events from last_seq + 1. Server maintains a ring buffer of the last 1000 events per org. If the gap is larger than 1000, client does a full sync_state instead.

Amendment 4.4: OTA Update Needs Client Notification

The gap: C4's OTA update system pushes skill updates to containers silently. C7's Academy and multi-user features mean clients may be in the middle of work when an update arrives. A hot update that changes a skill's behavior while a user is actively using it is confusing.

Amendment: Add update notification protocol:

  1. AOM pushes update signal to container
  2. Container broadcasts: { "type": "system_update", "update_type": "hot", "description": "New skills available", "applied_in": 5 } (5 second warning)
  3. Client UI shows a subtle toast: "Skills updating..." (not blocking, not alarming)
  4. After applied: { "type": "system_update_complete", "version": "v2026-03-16-003" }
  5. Toast updates: "Skills updated to latest version"

For warm and cold updates (which interrupt service), give 60-second and 5-minute warnings respectively.

Amendment 4.5: Container Resource Limits Need Dynamic Adjustment

The gap: C4 sets fixed resource limits: 2 cores, 4 GB RAM per container. C5 adds video content generation (Cleo). C7 adds video agents with GPU requirements. A fixed limit that works for text-based agents doesn't work for compute-intensive features.

Amendment: Introduce resource tier profiles:

Profile CPU RAM Use Case
standard 2 cores 4 GB Text agents, chat, tasks (C3-C4)
enhanced 4 cores 8 GB Content generation, Playwright QA (C5)
gpu-burst 4 cores + GPU 16 GB Video agents, vision tasks (C7)

Standard profile is the default. Enhanced activates when the container detects compute-heavy skills are installed. GPU-burst is on-demand: container requests GPU from the fleet manager when a video task starts, releases when done. This prevents paying for GPU when 95% of tasks are text-based.

Bobby doesn't need to build this in C4. But the container template should have a resource_profile field in its config so the fleet manager can swap profiles without rebuilding.

Amendment 4.6: Onboarding Flow Needs "Import Existing Business Data" Path

The gap: C4's onboarding assumes the client is starting fresh. They answer questions, and context files are generated from their answers. But C7's industry editions and multi-user suggest some clients will have existing data: a QuickBooks export, a client list CSV, an existing project tracker. The onboarding should accept imports.

Amendment: Add optional Step 4.5 between "Tell us about your business" and "Set your goals":

  • "Want to import existing data?" (skip if no)
  • Accept: CSV (client list, contact list), QuickBooks export, Google Contacts, spreadsheet (generic)
  • CC processes the import and populates context files + initial tasks from the imported data
  • "We found 47 clients, 12 active projects, and $34k in outstanding invoices. Sound right?" (confirmation)

This step is optional and can be skipped. But for clients with existing businesses (the majority), it dramatically reduces time-to-value.

C5 Amendments

Amendment 5.1: Self-Service Signup Needs Fraud Prevention

The gap: C5 removes the human gate from signup. Anyone with a credit card gets a container. But: stolen credit cards, trial abuse (sign up, use 7 days, cancel, repeat with new email), and competitors spinning up containers to study the product.

Amendment: Add fraud prevention layers:

  1. Stripe Radar: Enabled by default. Blocks high-risk cards. No code needed; Stripe handles it.
  2. Email verification: Before trial starts. Verify email is real. Block disposable email domains (mailinator, etc.).
  3. Trial fingerprinting: Device fingerprint (canvas, WebGL, screen resolution) stored on trial start. If the same fingerprint creates a new trial within 90 days, flag for review.
  4. Rate limiting: Max 3 trial signups per IP per day.
  5. Competitor detection: If a trial account doesn't send any chat messages within 48 hours (they're just looking at the UI), mark as "low engagement" and send a targeted onboarding email, not a container shutdown.

Most of this is Stripe Radar + basic checks. Not a significant build. But the spec should mention it.

Amendment 5.2: Furniture Marketplace Needs Gifting

The gap: C5's furniture marketplace lets clients buy packs for themselves. C7's neighbor offices and social layer make gifting a natural extension: "Send a gift pack to your neighbor." This drives engagement and creates viral loops. But the purchase flow in C5 doesn't support "buy for someone else."

Amendment: Add to the furniture purchase flow:

  • "Buy for myself" (default)
  • "Send as gift" (select neighbor from list, include optional message)
  • Recipient gets: in-app notification + the items appear in their inventory
  • Gift wrapping animation: items arrive in a box that unwraps in their office (Steffen designs)

This is a small addition to the Stripe checkout flow (different recipient org_id on the purchase record) but it should be designed into C5, not bolted on later.

Amendment 5.3: XP System Needs Anti-Gaming Protection

The gap: C5's XP system awards points for task completion, commits, and handoffs. A client could game the system: create 100 trivial tasks, check them off, farm XP. The leaderboard becomes meaningless if gaming is easy.

Amendment: Add anti-gaming heuristics:

  • Minimum task duration: Tasks completed within 10 seconds of creation earn 0 XP (autocomplete/spam)
  • Daily cap: Max 200 XP/day from task completions (20 tasks worth). Streaks and milestones are uncapped.
  • Agent-verified tasks: Only tasks that agents actually worked on (CC generated output) earn full XP. Manually checked-off tasks earn 5 XP instead of 10.
  • Diminishing returns: Same task text completed multiple times earns 50% less each time (prevents "complete, uncomplete, recomplete" cycling)

These rules are invisible to honest users. Only trigger for gaming patterns.

Amendment 5.4: Weekly Recap Needs "Share to Social" Format

The gap: C5's weekly recap is an in-app animation. C7 talks about shareable content. But the recap format isn't optimized for sharing. A Framer Motion animation can't be posted to LinkedIn. It needs an export format.

Amendment: Weekly recap should generate two shareable formats:

  1. Image card (1200x630px): Static summary card. Business name, week dates, key stats (tasks completed, hours saved, ROI), Corner branding. Optimized for LinkedIn/Twitter sharing.
  2. Video clip (15 seconds, 1080x1920px): Vertical video recap suitable for Instagram Stories/Reels. Auto-generated from the Framer Motion animation using Remotion (the content agent already uses this pipeline).

"Share my recap" button in the recap viewer. Opens share sheet on mobile, copy-link on desktop.

This is organic marketing. Every shared recap is a Corner ad. Free distribution.

Amendment 5.5: Skills Gallery Needs "Skills for Your Industry" Section

The gap: C5's skills gallery is a flat list with categories. C7's industry editions pre-configure skills by vertical. The gallery should surface industry-relevant skills prominently, not make clients browse the full catalog.

Amendment: Skills gallery should have a personalized "Recommended for You" section:

  • Based on client's industry (from onboarding Step 2)
  • Based on what agents they have installed
  • Based on what similar businesses use (cross-client data, anonymized)
  • "Construction companies like yours also use: Permit Tracker, Job Costing, Safety Checklist"

This leverages data that already exists in Supabase (onboarding answers, installed skills). The recommendation algorithm is simple: collaborative filtering based on industry + installed skill overlap.

Amendment 5.6: ROI Reports Need Configurable Value Assumptions

The gap: C5's ROI report calculates "value delivered" using a fixed hourly rate assumption. But a CPA's hour is worth $250. A contractor's office manager's hour is worth $35. The ROI report that uses a generic $50/hour is either wildly inflating value for one client or underreporting for another.

Amendment: During onboarding (or in Settings > ROI), ask:

  • "What's the approximate hourly cost of the work your AI team handles?" (dropdown: $25, $50, $75, $100, $150, $200, $250+, or custom)
  • Use this value in ROI calculations
  • ROI report shows the assumption: "Based on your configured rate of $150/hour, your AI team delivered $4,500 in value this month."
  • Allow monthly adjustment (businesses learn over time what the real value is)

This makes the ROI report credible. A CPA seeing "your team saved you 30 hours at $200/hour = $6,000" versus their $3,000 subscription is an instant retention win. But only if the number is real.

Amendment 5.7: Neighbor Offices Need Content Moderation for Guest Book

The gap: C5's neighbor offices include a guest book where visitors leave messages. No moderation system is specified. Internet + anonymous messages = inevitable abuse.

Amendment:

  • Profanity filter (C5 spec mentions this, good)
  • Rate limit: 1 guest book message per visitor per day per office
  • Report button on each guest book entry (flags for AOM review)
  • Auto-hide messages with 3+ reports
  • Office owner can delete any guest book entry
  • AOM admin can ban users from guest book across the platform
  • Guest book entries expire after 30 days (prevents accumulation)

Cross-Spec Amendments

Amendment X.1: Accessibility (Missing from All Specs)

The gap: None of the C3-C5 specs mention accessibility. Screen readers, keyboard-only navigation, color contrast, reduced motion preferences. The product spec's north star is "old people can't live without it." Old people have vision impairments, motor impairments, cognitive differences.

Amendment applies to all specs:

  • WCAG 2.1 AA compliance as a minimum standard
  • All interactive elements keyboard-accessible (Tab, Enter, Escape)
  • All images/icons have alt text (agent sprites, furniture, room elements)
  • Color is never the only way to convey information (status dots have icons too)
  • prefers-reduced-motion: disable all animations (character movement, handoff floats, weekly recap auto-play, zoom transitions). Show static equivalents.
  • prefers-contrast: increase contrast on all text and borders
  • Screen reader: all modes (Game, Checklist, Megaboard) have aria labels. The Game view has a screen-reader alternative (text description of room states). Checklist is naturally accessible. Megaboard's charts need alt text descriptions.
  • Font sizes: minimum 16px body text (already in brand guidelines). All text scalable with browser zoom up to 200%.

Bobby should apply these standards from C3 Step 1. Retrofitting accessibility is 10x harder than building it in.

Amendment X.2: Error Handling Philosophy (Inconsistent Across Specs)

The gap: C3 has detailed error handling for WebSocket (reconnection, SSE fallback). C4 has detailed error handling for provisioning. C5 has detailed error handling for Stripe. But there's no unified error handling philosophy. What does the user see when something breaks?

Amendment: Establish a single error handling pattern across all specs:

User-facing errors (things the client sees):

  • Never show technical details. Never show error codes. Never show stack traces.
  • Every error is a sentence in plain English: "Your connection was interrupted. Reconnecting now."
  • Every error has a clear action: "Try again", "Contact support", or nothing (self-resolving).
  • Errors are toasts or inline messages. Never full-screen error pages. Never block the entire UI.
  • Self-resolving errors (network drop, container restart) show status, not errors: "Reconnecting..." is a status. "Connection failed" is an error. Prefer statuses.

Logging errors (things AOM sees):

  • Every error logged to container's error.log with: timestamp, error type, stack trace, context (what the user was doing)
  • Critical errors (container crash, CC session death, data loss risk) trigger admin panel alert
  • Non-critical errors (network blip, WebSocket reconnect, rate limit) logged silently

Amendment X.3: Data Migration Strategy (Missing)

The gap: None of the specs discuss how to migrate data between spec versions. When C4 adds new Supabase tables, what happens to C3's data? When C5 changes the furniture JSON format, what happens to C3's furniture configs? When C7 adds assigned_to on tasks, what happens to C4 clients' existing tasks?

Amendment: Every spec version that changes the Supabase schema or data format MUST include:

  • A migration SQL script (Supabase migrations)
  • A rollback SQL script (undo the migration)
  • A data transformation script (convert existing data to new format)
  • Testing: migration script tested against a clone of production data before deployment

Bobby should establish a supabase/migrations/ directory in C3. Each spec version adds its migration file. Migrations run in order. Rollback is always possible.

Amendment X.4: Analytics/Telemetry Strategy (Missing)

The gap: C5 has trend charts and ROI reports for clients. But there's no product analytics for AOM. How does AOM know which features are used? Which modes are most popular? Where do users drop off in onboarding? What's the average session duration?

Amendment: AOM needs product analytics from C3 launch:

  • Tool: PostHog (self-hosted, GDPR compliant, free tier sufficient)
  • Events to track: page views, mode switches, chat messages sent, tasks created/completed, onboarding step completions, feature usage (which keyboard shortcuts, how often they zoom, Checklist vs Game vs Megaboard time)
  • User properties: plan tier, industry, agent count, days since signup
  • Privacy: no PII in analytics. Org ID and user ID only. No message content. No task text.
  • Dashboard: PostHog dashboard for AOM team showing: DAU, MAU, feature adoption, onboarding funnel, retention curves

This data feeds C7's predictive intelligence and C5's "what similar businesses use" recommendations. Start collecting from C3. Don't wait.

Bobby's immediate action items (before C3 build):

  1. Add protocol versioning to WebSocket (3.1)
  2. Add assigned_to, created_by to tasks schema (3.2)
  3. Add source, user_id to XP schema (3.3)
  4. Implement keyboard shortcut registry (3.4)
  5. Set up Supabase migrations directory (X.3)
  6. Install PostHog (X.4)
  7. Apply WCAG 2.1 AA standards from Step 1 (X.1)

These are all low-effort, high-value changes that prevent expensive retrofitting later.

Specs are living documents. The best time to catch a gap is before the first line of code. The second best time is now.
